system.description: The Dreamer walks the dreamscape with the rare ability to control their dreams and eventually the shared dream with others. In this world they understand the patterns of magic and are comparable to a Gray Witch in magical efficacy with their ability to work with animals, perform magical rituals, and eventually cast spells. A Dreamer's special type of dreaming gives them unique insights into the future, resulting in gifts of prophecy and prediction while awake. Dreamers learn to focus their abilities in such a way as to project both themselves and allies into the Plane of Dreams. As a Dreamer grows in power, they learns to create objects on the Plane of Dreams and eventually to draw those objects back to the waking worlds. They can call dream animals both onto the Plane of Dreams and the natural universe, and ultimately, even dream their own imagined animal into existence. Experienced Dreamers gain the power to summon non-allies into the Plane of Dreams, as well as summon beings from the Plane of Dreams back to the waking world. As their power grows even further, Dreamers can enchant animals, creatures, and objects that originate in the Plane of Dreams or that they have created there.

Explorers always wonder what's over the next hill, what's at the bottom of the deepest hole, what's at the end of the trail, or where is the next sea or the farthest shore. A heretic may be setting up a different branch of belief or just out to achieve ends the normal clergy would find anathema. Either way the heretic is a Rogue Priest, one who is often difficult to trust and hard to follow. They are not a shepherd of the flock, and if they take this role it is not held for long. Sometimes heretics will be found among the normal clergy but this is usually because they are trying to achieve some temporary goal. As such, Illuminators are strongest when on the Phase Plane and weakest when on the Shadow Plane. Their spellcasting ability is similar to that of a standard Mage, but every spell is lit with incandescence. Once an opponent realizes this fact, they are allowed to make an Illusion Resistance for half effect of the spell, removing the influence of phase. For the Illuminator, this weakness is offset by the ability to cast-and eventually master-all spells that involve light or fire without having to learn and memorize them. As for an Illuminator's mastery over fire, they are similar to a Kineticist in that they are adept at the additional abilities of Pyrokinesis. Eventually, when this Mage of illumination becomes a master of light and fire, wherever they go, they are surrounded by a shroud of fire causing it to be perpetually lit as if it were day.

These masters of physics forgo and eschew the casting of spells to tap into elemental and natural forces bound up with magic, which they employ directly for varied effects. system.description: The Luckster begins their career as a odds shaver, cheating to make their way. They continue as a huckster, charming their way with social manipulation. They use their innate magical gifts to bend luck in their favor. Eventually they learn to do this for their friends and against their enemies, becoming increasingly good at this until they cause nearly miraculous events to proceed. The Luckstrer can use their ability to store bad luck that occurs to them and eventually around them to later alter events to their advantage. Gambling is the Luckster's friend. They have a keen sense of when things are turning against them with Danger Knowledge. They also can see and identify magic. Late in their careers the Luckster learns to craft potions and scry. Their reliance on luck and magic makes them less reliant on other roguish staples like Street Knowledge, etc. as they count on their magic to handle these situations. Just being a Luckster's friend can be a boon while their enemies find that fate works against them.

system.description: When the time comes to cull the herd and remove the weak links. Someone must weed out the heretics, charlatans and true blasphemers. The Inquisitor revels in such efforts. The truth serves them. Lies serve them. The fear of death serves them and even death is not an escape for the powerful Inquisitor. They question even the recently dead. These fanatical priests cannot be reasoned with. They cannot be bribed. They see only the holy righteous fires of their fanatical cause. Nothing is too extreme for their cause. The loss of a few innocents or weaklings is not too high a price to pay for the strength of the faithful. Besides, they will be saved in the next life if they are truly worthy, but few are. They go after the very soul of their targets, using it against their foes. Even this is not too extreme and thus only rarely are they truly sanctioned by their deities in times when the faith is flagging and heretical teachings are on the rise. An Inquisitor can be good or evil as long as they are fanatical and have a cause to serve.
